title: List of prime ministers of the United Kingdom
summary: This document is a partial version of the Wikipedia article "List of prime ministers of the United Kingdom." It provides historical context about the office of prime minister, explaining that the role evolved gradually rather than being formally created, with the term used informally by Robert Walpole in the 1730s and only becoming an official title in 1905 under Henry Campbell-Bannerman. It identifies key historical milestones, including Robert Walpole as the first and longest-serving prime minister, William Pitt the Younger as the first PM of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland, Benjamin Disraeli as the first to use the title in an official act, and Andrew Bonar Law as the first PM of the current United Kingdom. The document traces the origins of the role back before the 1707 union, describing the Lord High Treasurer of England (with figures like William Cecil and Sidney Godolphin) and the Chancellor of Scotland. It also covers the transitional period from 1707 to 1721, when figures such as Charles Townshend, Lords Stanhope and Sunderland governed before Walpole's tenure established the precedent that the first lord of the Treasury typically served as prime minister. Additionally, the document addresses disputed prime ministers, specifically William Pulteney, Earl of Bath, and James Waldegrave, whose brief failed attempts to form governments in 1746 and 1757 are not recognized by modern academic consensus. The article concludes with placeholder sections for a timeline of prime ministers, references, and external links to government and BBC resources.
